body: The future is not predetermined, and nothing is inevitable. We are at this time in the situation described by Gramsci that so many people have of late cited, and with good reason: “The crisis consists precisely in the fact that the old way is dying and the new cannot be born; in this interregnum a great variety of morbid symptoms appear.” We do not know which future we are living in precisely because the battle for the future is being waged at this very time. Nonetheless, as Raskin also observes, correctly in my view, the Barbarization scenario has gained significant ground over the past two decades at the expense of Conventional Worlds, whereas Great Transition scenarios have made considerably less headway. capitalist states face spiraling crises of legitimacy, and the system is rapidly losing its ideological hegemony
Crises are times of escalating social and political conflict
. They are also times when the variables that help us make sense of things are most fluid and great uncertainty hangs in the balance.
What is certain is that the existing state of affairs cannot be sustained
, but exactly what that change will involve is not yet clear.
